correctness.rationale: For every odd prime power q, the normalized associative commutator reduces exactly to u∧v+u∧d+c∧v with u,v∈F_q^4 and c,d∈Λ^3(F_q^4), with q^16 freely chosen even components. Nonzero simple bivectors have q(q²−1) ordered wedge lifts and the top-degree linear functional has q^7 solutions for each target. The zero bivector has q^5+q^4−q dependent-vector lifts, exactly one of which yields only top scalar zero. Pfaffian rank gives exhaustive bivector cases, and rank0/1/4 kernels give centralizers and zero fiber. Rank-four bivectors require two simple summands and provide a width-two obstruction. Actual packaged verify.py was run and returned VERIFY_OK on full bivector enumerations q=3,5 and full odd-part rank q=3; checks are finite corroboration only. Characteristic two and generator rank beyond four are excluded.

value.rationale: The image and each point fiber of the natural associative commutator map are complete ring invariants; at four generators they first exhibit a nondecomposable Klein-quadric obstruction even though the linear commutator subspace is all of Λ²⊕Λ⁴. The exact two-commutator width, sharp transition, uniform finite-field fiber counts, and full centralizer spectrum are meaningful natural classification data, not a chosen arbitrary slice or a recomputation of classical Plucker point counts alone. They quantify the difference between the linear commutator span and pointwise word image and determine the exact finite-field commuting probability; no downstream theorem is asserted.
